title: Wreck and Summit
premise: Oscar Vane, a salvage diver and digger who has spent a decade outrunning her mother's shadow, is hired as a last-minute replacement on an upriver expedition led by the archaeologist she hasn't spoken to in nine years. When the camp goes silent, Oscar goes after them alone and finds the team trapped by floodwater, a rival salvage crew, and a discovery — a pre-colonial burial city — that governments and looters would kill to control. To bring the survivors home, Oscar must choose between exposing the find and honoring her mother's dying wish that it stay buried; she chooses a third path, smuggling the evidence to the descendant communities of the valley so they can claim it themselves. In the end she loses the river's treasure but gains something she never planned: a reason to stop moving.
about_author: Ulyana Winterbourne is a former river guide who spent six seasons on remote waterways before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about people who are better at leaving than staying.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Oscar Vane dives a flooded quarry for a salvage outfit, methodically erasing herself from every record she can. A telegram arrives: her estranged mother, Dr. Iris Vane, needs a digger for one season, no questions asked. POV Oscar. Beat: restless competence masking grief.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Oscar travels upriver by steamer, rehearsing and discarding apologies. Flashbacks reveal the fight that split them: Iris chose a dig over Oscar's father's funeral. She arrives at basecamp and mother and daughter exchange only logistics. POV Oscar. Beat: cold formality over old wounds.

chapters.title: Basecamp Rules
chapters.summary: Iris runs the expedition like a fortress: radio schedules, supply counts, a strict no-artifacts-out policy. Oscar proves herself fast, earning wary respect from the young crew, especially botanist Teo Reyes, who asks too many kind questions. POV Oscar. Beat: grudging belonging.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: A sonar anomaly leads the team to terraced stone beneath the floodplain. Iris orders it mapped but not touched, which puzzles everyone — Iris Vane has never left a site unopened. Oscar notices her mother is afraid. POV Oscar. Beat: first crack in the mystery.

chapters.title: The Other Boat
chapters.summary: An unmarked launch shadows the expedition; its pilot, Corliss Hale, claims to be a surveyor but carries salvage winches and a government letter with a redacted seal. Iris burns a page of her own field journal that night. POV Oscar. Beat: threat arrives wearing a smile.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Iris takes four people up a tributary to verify the site's extent, leaving Oscar at basecamp. The scheduled check-in comes and goes. Then all channels go dead, and storm clouds stack over the headwaters. POV Oscar. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Nobody's Permission
chapters.summary: The remaining crew wants to wait for authorities; Oscar calculates the flood will reach the tributary in three days and the authorities in ten. She requisitions the skiff and leaves alone at dawn, breaking every rule her mother ever taught her about safety. POV Oscar. Beat: commitment.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Oscar fights rapids, portages through leech country, and finds Hale's launch moored ahead of her — he's following the same trail. She sabotages his fuel line, buying a day she may not be able to afford. POV Oscar. Beat: ruthless pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Drowned Staircase
chapters.summary: Following Iris's marked blazes, Oscar finds the tributary camp abandoned, tents slashed, and a staircase descending into a cavern behind a waterfall. Inside: carvings of a city that predates anything in the literature. POV Oscar. Beat: awe tangled with fear.

chapters.title: Voices in the Dark
chapters.summary: Deep in the cavern system Oscar hears hammering — Morse, her mother's old field code. She answers. The trapped party is alive but pinned by rising water two chambers in, one member injured. POV Oscar. Beat: hope with a clock attached.

chapters.title: Reunion Under Pressure
chapters.summary: Oscar reaches them: Iris, Teo, and two others, rationing air and light. Mother and daughter finally speak honestly — Iris confesses she found this site years ago and buried the report because the last time a valley was 'protected,' its people were displaced. POV Oscar. Beat: love against duty, stated aloud.

chapters.title: Hale's Bargain
chapters.summary: Hale catches up, offering extraction for everyone if Iris signs over the find to his backers. He reveals the redacted letter: a state antiquities bureau that plans a dam, drowning the valley and erasing the descendants' claim forever. POV Oscar. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Refusing the bargain, they attempt the underwater sump Oscar spotted — the only route out before the flood peaks. Oscar teaches the others her diving techniques; the injured man cannot make the swim. POV Oscar. Beat: impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: What We Leave Behind
chapters.summary: The injured crew member, Marta, chooses to stay with the artifacts and hold the cavern, buying the others time. Her goodbye reframes the mission: not rescue, but witness. POV Oscar. Beat: sacrifice without melodrama.

chapters.title: The Sump
chapters.summary: The dive sequence: blackout dark, snagged lines, Teo nearly drowns and Oscar drags him through. They surface outside the waterfall as the flood swallows the lower chambers behind them. POV Oscar. Beat: survival paid for in terror.

chapters.title: Downriver, Running
chapters.summary: Hale pursues with armed men; the survivors scatter through the rainforest toward a mission settlement where descendants of the valley still live. Iris collapses — she's been hiding a heart condition. POV Oscar. Beat: flight, and role reversal.

chapters.title: The Keepers
chapters.summary: At the settlement, elder Rosa Anco recognizes the site from oral tradition: it is her people's ancestral city, taken by flood legend long ago. Oscar realizes the artifacts' true owners were never the bureau or Hale. POV Oscar. Beat: justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Thieves
chapters.summary: Oscar returns upstream alone to retrieve the documentation Iris hid in the caverns, while Hale's men occupy the site. She steals the records out from under them and torches their fuel cache. POV Oscar. Beat: the better digger becomes the better thief.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Cornered at the rising river, Oscar bargains with Hale using what he can't fake: proof that his backers' dam permit rests on a falsified survey. She trades silence for the crew's safe passage downriver. POV Oscar. Beat: climax — wit over force.

chapters.title: Marta's Light
chapters.summary: Rescuers reach the cavern; Marta is alive, having sheltered in a high gallery with the artifacts intact. The reunion is quiet and shaken. Iris, hospitalized downriver, formally withdraws her name from any publication. POV Oscar. Beat: cost counted, mercy found.

chapters.title: The Claim
chapters.summary: Rosa Anco's community files a heritage claim backed by the smuggled records; the dam review stalls, then fails. The valley stays whole, its city still buried by choice. Hale's backers implode quietly. POV Oscar. Beat: justice done without applause.

chapters.title: Where the Water Slows
chapters.summary: Months later, Oscar stands at the confluence where the tributary meets the main river, holding her mother's old compass. Iris asks her to co-lead a stewardship program with the Anco community. For the first time, Oscar unpacks everything she owns. POV Oscar. Beat: memory honored, movement ended.
